drivingQuestion: How much of the blood must be covered, and what reading of the word דמו underlies the three tannaitic positions?
outcomeNote: The sugya locates the three-way dispute in three readings of the word דמו; it does not decide between them.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״וְכִסָּהוּ״ – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל דָּמוֹ חַיָּיב לְכַסּוֹת, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: דָּם הַנִּיתָּז וְשֶׁעַל אֲגַפַּיִים חַיָּיב לְכַסּוֹת. אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים – שֶׁלֹּא כִּסָּה דַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ, אֲבָל כִּסָּה דַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ – פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת.
segments.en: «It is taught» in «another» baraita: The term: «“And he shall cover it,” teaches that» one is «obligated to cover all» of the «blood. From here» the Sages «stated:» With regard to «blood that spurts out and» blood «that» remains «on the sides» of the animal’s throat where it was slaughtered, one is «obligated to cover» it. «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: In what» case «is this statement said?» It is said in a case «where» one «did not» already «cover the blood of the soul,» i.e., the blood that flows from the place of slaughter as the animal dies. «But if» one already «covered the blood of the soul,» he is «exempt from» the obligation «to cover» the blood that spurted out or the blood remaining on the sides of the animal’s neck in the area of slaughter.

segments.he: בְּמַאי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי? רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: ״דָּמוֹ״ – כׇּל דָּמוֹ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: ״דָּמוֹ״ – וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת דָּמוֹ, וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: ״דָּמוֹ״ – הַמְיוּחָד.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «With regard to what» matter «do they disagree?» The Gemara responds: «The Rabbis hold» that the expression: «“Its blood”» (Leviticus 17:13), indicates an obligation to cover «all of its blood,» even the blood that spurts out. «Rabbi Yehuda holds» that «“its blood”» indicates that one may fulfill the mitzva with any part of the blood, «even» with «a small amount of its blood. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds» that «“its blood”» refers to the «special» blood, i.e., the blood of the soul.
